title: What Plasma Sodium Reports
endLine: Plasma sodium reports cation per litre of water, not body sodium.

scenes.tts: Last time, water crossed between two rooms until every litre held the same number of stuck guests. Now a blood test reads low plasma sodium. Has this body lost sodium?
scenes.narration: Last time, water crossed between two rooms until every litre held the same number of stuck guests. Now a blood test reads low plasma sodium. Has this body lost sodium?
scenes.caption: Last time, water crossed between two rooms until every litre held the same number of stuck guests. Now a blood test reads low plasma sodium. Has this body lost sodium?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map without a reset. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as before: BLUE = water (water dots, the 'water only' door); GREEN = inside cells (ICF room, left, wide, labelled '28 L'); ORANGE = outside cells (ECF room, right, half as wide, labelled '14 L'); YELLOW = effective solute (stuck solute chips: in the GREEN room they are potassium salts, in the ORANGE room sodium salts); GOLD = question marks and the title rule; GREY = the cell membrane with the BLUE door in its middle. The two rooms fill about 65% of the frame height. NEW in this film and kept all film: a round WHITE dial above the ORANGE room labelled 'plasma sodium', a YELLOW needle, a digital readout under it in mmol per L, starting at 140. Recap motion on the first sentence: BLUE water dots pass through the door both ways and settle; YELLOW chips in both rooms jiggle in place, none crossing. On 'low plasma sodium', the needle swings down and the readout blinks 'low'. On the question, a large GOLD question mark appears beside the dial, and text across the top: 'Lost sodium?'. Ambient: water dots drift slowly in both rooms all film.
Title 'What Plasma Sodium Reports' fades in above the rooms for 2 s while the question text fades out. The needle eases back to 140. Water dots keep drifting.

scenes.tts: Plasma sodium is a concentration: sodium per litre of water. So the reading has two parts, the sodium and the water it sits in. Change either one, and the needle moves.
scenes.narration: Plasma sodium is a concentration: sodium per litre of water. So the reading has two parts, the sodium and the water it sits in. Change either one, and the needle moves.
scenes.caption: Plasma sodium is a concentration: sodium per litre of water. So the reading has two parts, the sodium and the water it sits in. Change either one, and the needle moves.
scenes.visual: Under the dial a simple fraction builds: YELLOW 'sodium' on top, BLUE 'water' below, a WHITE bar between. On 'the sodium', the top word pulses and a few YELLOW chips in the ORANGE room pulse with it; on 'the water it sits in', the bottom word pulses and the BLUE dots in the ORANGE room shimmer. On 'Change either one', the needle wobbles once down and back up. The fraction stays under the dial for the rest of the film.

scenes.tts: Take the litre of solute free water again. No sodium left the body. But the litre spread through all body water, and diluted the sodium outside cells. In the model, plasma sodium falls from one hundred forty to about one hundred thirty six point seven millimoles per litre.
scenes.narration: Take the litre of solute-free water again. No sodium left the body. But the litre spread through all body water, and diluted the sodium outside cells. In the model, plasma sodium falls from 140 to about 136.7 mmol per L.
scenes.caption: Take the litre of solute-free water again. No sodium left the body. But the litre spread through all body water, and diluted the sodium outside cells. In the model, plasma sodium falls from 140 to about 136.7 mmol per L.
scenes.visual: A BLUE 1 L block drops into the ORANGE room and dissolves into dots; BLUE dots pass the door so that two-thirds settle in the GREEN room and one-third stays in the ORANGE room (the first film's split; room labels update to '28.67 L' and '14.33 L'). The YELLOW sodium chips in the ORANGE room do not change in number; a small tag beside them reads 'no sodium lost'. On 'diluted', the chips spread slightly further apart. The BLUE 'water' word in the fraction grows a little; the needle slides from 140 to 136.7, computed as 140 x 42 / 43. Tag under the readout: 'model, rounded numbers'.

scenes.tts: Now a stranger case, as bookkeeping. Remove six hundred milliosmoles of potassium salts from the cells, and from the body. Not one sodium ion leaves. Does plasma sodium rise, fall, or stay the same?
scenes.narration: Now a stranger case, as bookkeeping. Remove 600 mOsm of potassium salts from the cells, and from the body. Not one sodium ion leaves. Does plasma sodium rise, fall, or stay the same?
scenes.caption: Now a stranger case, as bookkeeping. Remove 600 mOsm of potassium salts from the cells, and from the body. Not one sodium ion leaves. Does plasma sodium rise, fall, or stay the same?
scenes.visual: Reset the rooms to the start: GREEN '28 L', ORANGE '14 L', needle at 140. A tag at top left: 'bookkeeping'. On 'Remove', a cluster of YELLOW potassium-salt chips in the GREEN room lifts out through the top of the room and leaves the frame, labelled '600 mOsm potassium salts'. On 'Not one sodium ion leaves', the YELLOW sodium chips in the ORANGE room glow once and stay put. Question card at top in white: 'Rise, fall, or stay?'. The needle waits at 140; rooms keep their size.
Predict pause. The question card stays. The rooms hold their size; BLUE dots drift; the needle trembles slightly at 140. No other change.

scenes.tts: It falls. Potassium salts are the cells' stuck guests. With fewer of them, cells hold less water. In the model, cells shrink from twenty eight to about twenty seven point three litres. That water moves outside.
scenes.narration: It falls. Potassium salts are the cells' stuck guests. With fewer of them, cells hold less water. In the model, cells shrink from 28 to about 27.3 L. That water moves outside.
scenes.caption: It falls. Potassium salts are the cells' stuck guests. With fewer of them, cells hold less water. In the model, cells shrink from 28 to about 27.3 L. That water moves outside.
scenes.visual: Question card dissolves into the word 'falls'. On 'fewer of them', the remaining YELLOW chips in the GREEN room pulse. BLUE dots stream through the door from the GREEN room to the ORANGE room; the GREEN room narrows and its label counts 28 to 27.3 L. Numbers computed from the lesson: common concentration 12,000 / 42 = 285.7 mOsm per kg; cells 7,800 / 285.7 = 27.3 L.

scenes.tts: Fluid outside cells rises to about fourteen point seven litres. Plasma sodium falls from one hundred forty to about one hundred thirty three. No sodium was lost. Real potassium depletion is messier, but the body still loses effective solute. So plasma sodium still falls.
scenes.narration: Fluid outside cells rises to about 14.7 L. Plasma sodium falls from 140 to about 133. No sodium was lost. Real potassium depletion is messier, but the body still loses effective solute. So plasma sodium still falls.
scenes.caption: Fluid outside cells rises to about 14.7 L. Plasma sodium falls from 140 to about 133. No sodium was lost. Real potassium depletion is messier, but the body still loses effective solute. So plasma sodium still falls.
scenes.visual: The ORANGE room widens and its label counts 14 to 14.7 L; its YELLOW sodium chips spread apart, same number. The BLUE 'water' word in the fraction grows; the needle slides from 140 to 133, computed as 140 x 14 / 14.7. Tag beside the chips: 'no sodium lost'. On 'messier', a small tag 'real life: messier' appears at top left over the 'bookkeeping' tag; on 'still falls', the needle stays low and the tag dims.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea. Plasma sodium tracks all the exchangeable cation, sodium and potassium, per litre of body water. It is a ratio of cation to water. It is not a gauge of the body's sodium stock.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea. Plasma sodium tracks all the exchangeable cation, sodium and potassium, per litre of body water. It is a ratio of cation to water. It is not a gauge of the body's sodium stock.
scenes.caption: Here is the idea. Plasma sodium tracks all the exchangeable cation, sodium and potassium, per litre of body water. It is a ratio of cation to water. It is not a gauge of the body's sodium stock.
scenes.visual: The fraction under the dial transforms: the top word 'sodium' becomes 'sodium + potassium', and the bottom word 'water' becomes 'all body water'. YELLOW chips in BOTH rooms pulse together on 'sodium and potassium'; BLUE dots in both rooms shimmer on 'per litre of body water'. On 'not a gauge of the body's sodium stock', a YELLOW pile of chips labelled 'sodium stock' appears beside the dial with a GREY line struck through the link between them.

scenes.tts: In nineteen fifty eight, Isidore Edelman and colleagues tested this in ninety eight chronically ill patients. In most, they measured exchangeable sodium, exchangeable potassium and total body water by isotope dilution. Exchangeable means the part of each store that mixes with an injected isotope.
scenes.narration: In 1958, Isidore Edelman and colleagues tested this in 98 chronically ill patients. In most, they measured exchangeable sodium, exchangeable potassium and total body water by isotope dilution. Exchangeable means the part of each store that mixes with an injected isotope.
scenes.caption: In 1958, Isidore Edelman and colleagues tested this in 98 chronically ill patients. In most, they measured exchangeable sodium, exchangeable potassium and total body water by isotope dilution. Exchangeable means the part of each store that mixes with an injected isotope.
scenes.visual: The rooms shrink to the left 40% of the frame, still drifting; the dial stays above them. On the right, a tag 'Edelman, 1958, 98 patients'. Three plain stores appear as labelled tanks, no molecular detail: a YELLOW 'body sodium' tank, a YELLOW 'body potassium' tank and a BLUE 'body water' tank. On 'mixes with an injected isotope', a few bright WHITE tracer dots are dropped into the sodium tank and spread through its upper part, which gains the label 'exchangeable sodium'; a darker band at its base labelled 'does not mix' stays unreached.

scenes.tts: Serum sodium correlated poorly with any single store. It followed sodium plus potassium per litre of body water, with a correlation coefficient of zero point eight three. Patients with edema, carrying excess body sodium, could still have low plasma sodium.
scenes.narration: Serum sodium correlated poorly with any single store. It followed sodium plus potassium per litre of body water, with a correlation coefficient of 0.83. Patients with edema, carrying excess body sodium, could still have low plasma sodium.
scenes.caption: Serum sodium correlated poorly with any single store. It followed sodium plus potassium per litre of body water, with a correlation coefficient of 0.83. Patients with edema, carrying excess body sodium, could still have low plasma sodium.
scenes.visual: The three tanks become the fraction: the exchangeable parts of the two YELLOW tanks merge on top, the BLUE tank below. Beside it a plot: x axis 'cation per litre water', y axis 'serum sodium', no tick numbers. A straight WHITE line drawn from the lesson's fitted equation, y = 1.11 x - 25.6, with a loose cloud of dots around it tagged 'schematic points, r = 0.83'. On 'any single store', a faint flat cloud with no clear trend flashes briefly beside the sodium tank alone, tagged 'single store: poor' (schematic). On 'edema', one dot near the lower-left end of the line glows, tagged 'edema: high sodium stock'.

scenes.tts: Keep the limits. This is a correlation in sick patients, not an experiment. And exchangeable cation is not total cation, because much bone sodium does not exchange.
scenes.narration: Keep the limits. This is a correlation in sick patients, not an experiment. And exchangeable cation is not total cation, because much bone sodium does not exchange.
scenes.caption: Keep the limits. This is a correlation in sick patients, not an experiment. And exchangeable cation is not total cation, because much bone sodium does not exchange.
scenes.visual: The plot stays. On 'correlation in sick patients', a tag 'correlation, not experiment' appears above it. On 'bone sodium', the darker 'does not mix' band at the base of the sodium tank returns, relabelled 'bone sodium', and glows once.

scenes.tts: So a low plasma sodium means too much water for the cation present. By itself, it does not show whether body sodium is low, normal or high.
scenes.narration: So a low plasma sodium means too much water for the cation present. By itself, it does not show whether body sodium is low, normal or high.
scenes.caption: So a low plasma sodium means too much water for the cation present. By itself, it does not show whether body sodium is low, normal or high.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full two-room world at full size, dial above, needle low. On 'too much water', the BLUE 'water' word in the fraction swells and BLUE dots in both rooms shimmer. On 'low, normal or high', three small YELLOW 'sodium stock' piles appear beside the dial, small, medium and large, each tagged 'low', 'normal', 'high'; all three connect to the same low needle with equal WHITE lines. The GOLD question mark from the opening returns and fades.

End card over the dimmed but still moving two-room world (BLUE dots drifting, YELLOW chips jiggling, needle resting). Large white text, centred: 'Plasma sodium reports cation per litre of water, not body sodium.'
